what: T1XFER complete: six clips, two adoptions, one rank point, box deleted

e28.note: worst clip on the board; object held to frame 745 of 988 against 118 shipped

e19.note: held to frame 437 of 886 against 133 shipped

e14.note: the largest AUC gain of all six, +0.2669, and still correctly refused

what_it_delivered: Tier 1 entry 0.52687 -> 0.53525 AUC, SP-SR 0.66667 -> 0.70000, MPPE 13.90 -> 12.20, and tier1-mppe 11th -> 10th confirmed on the live board. $2.23 of credit.
the_e14_case_is_the_most_instructive: +0.2669 of AUC, the biggest single-clip gain the arm produced, and adopting it would have been rank-NEUTRAL: entry AUC 0.54415 passes wte09fl (+1 rank on tier1-auc) while SP-SR falls 0.70000 -> 0.66667 and drops us out of a three-way tie (-1 rank), because the clip's MPPE going 6.06 -> 16.96 cm takes it from passing the 10 cm SP-SR gate to failing it. I checked this expecting to find my per-clip rule too strict; it agrees exactly with the board-level test.
three_selection_hypotheses_refuted: loses-vs-holds the object, inertia error, and donor-target size. The last was registered publicly as a prediction for e01 and e14 and both refuted it -- e01 at ratio 1.24 sits between two adoptions and failed. I cannot predict which clips work.
the_recommendation_that_survives: Run it on everything unadopted without selecting. 2 of 6 adopted for +0.2514 of summed AUC = +0.042 per clip tried = +0.0014 of entry AUC per $0.50 clip. The twelve remaining unadopted clips are about $6 for ~+0.017 of entry AUC, against the +0.0066 that separates us from wte09fl. A failed clip costs only its $0.50 because the no-regression rule keeps it out of the entry.
box: v2d-t1pilot deleted at 09:32 after all six rollouts were pulled and scored locally
